subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
title: Grammar in Use: Word Classes (Nouns)
overview: Nouns name people, places and things. Many nouns show "more than one" by adding a letter or two. Others change in their own way. In this sub-strand you will form plurals of regular and irregular nouns and use them in sentences about celebrations.

lessons.title: Plurals of regular nouns
objectives: Explain what a regular plural is.
Add -s or -es, and change y to ies, to make regular plurals.
Pick regular plurals out of a short celebration text.
lessons.intro: One balloon is easy to count. A room full of them needs a different form of the word. We say balloons, not balloon twice. That extra sound tells the listener there is more than one.
lessons.notes:
### One and more than one
A singular noun means one: cake, gift, child. A plural noun means more than one: cakes, gifts, children. You show the number of things partly by choosing singular or plural.

A regular noun makes its plural in a pattern you can learn and use again.

### Add -s
Most nouns add -s.

- cake → cakes
- gift → gifts
- balloon → balloons
- card → cards
- song → songs
- ribbon → ribbons
- wedding → weddings
- prize → prizes

If the noun ends in a vowel plus y, keep the y and add -s: boy → boys, day → days, toy → toys, birthday → birthdays. The letter before y in birthday is a, a vowel, so the y stays.

### Add -es
If the noun ends in s, x, ch or sh, add -es, because the extra syllable makes the word easier to say.

- glass → glasses
- box → boxes
- church → churches
- dish → dishes
- class → classes

You hear the extra part: box-es, church-es, dish-es.

### Change y to ies
If a consonant comes just before y, change y to i and add -es.

- baby → babies
- family → families
- party → parties
- ceremony → ceremonies

Party does not become partys. The consonant t sits before y, so the plural is parties.

### A special spelling to learn beside the pattern
Some nouns ending in f or fe change f to v and add -es: leaf → leaves, knife → knives, wife → wives. They are not a simple -s plural, so learn each one. Not every f word changes. Roof becomes roofs, and chief becomes chiefs.

### Hear them in a text
The families carried boxes of cakes and dishes of food. The parties had balloons, songs and prizes. Two birthdays fell in the same week, so the boys shared their toys.

Regular plurals in that text: families, boxes, cakes, dishes, parties, balloons, songs, prizes, birthdays, boys, toys.

When you listen to a passage, write the plural you hear, then ask which rule made it.

keyWords.meaning: the form of a noun that means one
the form of a noun that means more than one
a noun whose plural follows a common pattern such as adding -s or -es

examples.problem: Write the plurals of party, birthday, box and balloon.
steps: Party ends in consonant + y, so parties.
Birthday ends in vowel + y, so birthdays.
Box ends in x, so boxes.
Balloon adds -s: balloons.
Party ends in y.
The letter before y is t, a consonant.
Change y to i and add -es.
examples.answer: The plural of party is parties.

activity.title: Sort the regular plurals
materials: Word cards: cake, glass, baby, boy, ceremony, dish, birthday, prize
Three headings: add -s, add -es, y to ies
steps: In a group, give an example of a regular noun and say its plural.
Place each card under the correct heading and write the plural.
Discuss how these patterns differ from a noun such as child, which you will meet in the next lesson.
Listen as the teacher reads the short text in the notes. Write every regular plural you hear.

practice.question: Write the plurals: song, church, family, toy.
Which rule makes ceremony into ceremonies?
practice.answer: The y comes after a consonant, so change y to i and add -es.

practice.question: Write the plural of knife and the plural of roof.
From this list, write only the regular plurals: cakes, children, boxes, men.

summary: Add -es after s, x, ch or sh.
Consonant + y becomes ies. Vowel + y just adds -s.

lessons.title: Plurals of irregular nouns
objectives: Explain how irregular plurals differ from regular ones.
Use both kinds of plural in spoken and written sentences.
lessons.intro: If regular nouns followed the only rule in English, two children would be two childs, and two men would be two mans. Listeners would be confused, because those words have their own plural forms.
lessons.notes:
### What makes a noun irregular
An irregular noun does not make its plural by a simple -s or -es. The word itself changes, or it does not change at all. You learn these plurals by remembering them, then you use them until they sound natural.

### Nouns that change their vowel or their shape
- man → men
- woman → women
- child → children
- tooth → teeth
- foot → feet
- mouse → mice
- goose → geese
- person → people

There is no letter s at the end of men, women, feet, teeth, mice or geese. Children and people end in other ways. People is the usual plural of person.

### Nouns that stay the same
- sheep → sheep
- deer → deer

One sheep, many sheep. The number shows in other words: one sheep, five sheep. Fish often stays fish when you mean individual fish: three fish. Fishes can mean different kinds of fish. At Grade 4, use fish for more than one fish unless your teacher asks for kinds.

### Do not mix the two systems
Say children, not childs. Say men, not mans. Say feet, not foots. Say parties for the regular noun party, but people for the irregular noun person.

A celebration sentence can hold both kinds:

- The children blew up balloons for the parties.
- Two men and three women carried the boxes of cakes.
- The people at the feast washed their hands before they ate.

### Using them when you speak and write
Read the sentence and listen for the number. If you mean more than one, the noun must be plural even when another word already shows the number. "Many child" is not correct. Many already means more than one, and the noun still changes: many children.

"One of the men" is singular in meaning because one is singular, but men stays plural because you are picking one out of a group of men.

When you are unsure, look the noun up in a dictionary. The entry often shows the plural.

keyWords.meaning: a noun whose plural does not follow the usual -s or -es pattern
a plural that is spelled like the singular, such as sheep

examples.problem: Write the plurals of child, man, tooth and sheep.
steps: Child becomes children.
Man becomes men.
Tooth becomes teeth.
Sheep stays sheep.

examples.problem: Correct the sentence: The childs put the knifes near the foots of the guests.
steps: Child is irregular: children.
Knife changes f to v: knives.
Foot is irregular: feet.
examples.answer: The children put the knives near the feet of the guests.

activity.title: Hear the plurals
materials: A short list read aloud by the teacher
steps: Discuss with your group how a regular plural such as cakes differs from an irregular plural such as children.
Listen to this list and write only the plurals: men, cake, women, parties, teeth, balloon, people, sheep, boxes, feet.
Mark each plural R for regular or I for irregular.
Say a sentence that uses one regular plural and one irregular plural about a family feast.

practice.question: Write the plurals: woman, person, foot, deer.
Correct this phrase: many childs and two mans.
Use children and balloons in one sentence.
practice.answer: Any correct sentence, for example: The children tied balloons along the wall.

practice.question: Why is sheep the plural of sheep?
practice.answer: Sheep is an irregular noun whose plural has the same form as the singular.

summary: Irregular plurals do not simply add -s.
Learn men, women, children, teeth, feet, mice, geese and people.
Sheep and deer stay the same in the plural.

lessons.title: Using plurals and making a noun puzzle
objectives: Choose regular or irregular plurals when speaking and writing.
Make a puzzle that other learners can solve.
Encourage others to use the correct plural.
lessons.intro: Knowing a list is only half the job. In a real sentence about a wedding or a birthday, you have to choose the plural while you are talking or writing, without a table in front of you.
lessons.notes:
### Choose, then use
Ask two questions about every noun.

1. Do I mean one, or more than one?
2. If I mean more than one, is the noun regular or irregular?

One party, many parties. One child, many children. One glass, many glasses. One woman, many women.

### Sentences you can trust
- The families brought dishes and boxes of food.
- The men, the women and the children sang songs.
- We saw five sheep near the church after the ceremony.
- My feet were tired, but my teeth still had room for cake.

Read them aloud. The plurals should sound ordinary, not like a test. If childs or mans appears, stop and repair the word before you go on.

### A puzzle that teaches
A puzzle makes a friend think. Here is a simple kind.

Clues across a small grid, or just a numbered list:

1. Plural of child. (children)
2. More than one party. (parties)
3. Plural of sheep. (sheep)
4. More than one glass. (glasses)
5. Plural of man. (men)

You can also mix letters: scramble nem for men, or seixob for boxes. The solver writes the plural, not the singular.

When you make the puzzle, include both regular and irregular nouns so the solver practises the difference. Solve someone else's puzzle before you say yours is ready. If a clue has two possible answers, rewrite the clue.

### Help the plural spread
Correcting a friend is useful when you are kind. Say the right word in a sentence rather than only saying "wrong". "We need more chairs for the children" teaches the plural better than a frown.

Look up two nouns on a dictionary site or app your teacher chooses. Write the plural the dictionary gives. If the internet is not available, use a print dictionary. Share the two plurals with the class so more people can use them.

Using the right plural makes a celebration story clear. "The people ate cakes" tells you there was more than one person and more than one cake. "The person ate cake" tells a different story.

keyWords.meaning: a hint that helps someone find an answer
to mix up the letters of a word
a pattern of squares in which puzzle answers can be written

examples.problem: Choose the correct sentence: (a) The womans cut the cakes. (b) The women cut the cakes.
steps: More than one woman is meant.
The plural of woman is women, not womans.
Cakes is a regular plural and is already correct in both.

examples.problem: Write a puzzle clue for the plural of tooth, and give the answer.
steps: The clue should not give the spelling away.
The plural is irregular.
examples.answer: Clue: the plural of tooth. Answer: teeth.

activity.title: Plural puzzle
materials: A dictionary, print or digital, if the teacher allows
steps: Each pair lists five regular nouns and five irregular nouns about home, school or celebrations.
Look up any plural you are unsure of.
Write a puzzle of eight clues. Mix regular and irregular nouns.
Exchange puzzles with another pair and solve them.
Say two of the answers in full sentences so the class hears the plurals used properly.

practice.question: Correct the paragraph: Two mans and three childs carried boxs of cake to the partys.
practice.answer: Two men and three children carried boxes of cakes to the parties.

practice.question: Write a sentence using people and sheep correctly.
practice.answer: Any correct sentence, for example: The people counted five sheep after the feast.

practice.question: Give one regular plural and one irregular plural, and say which is which.
practice.answer: Any correct pair, for example: balloons is regular and children is irregular.

practice.question: Why should a puzzle include both kinds of noun?
practice.answer: So the solver practises the difference between adding -s or -es and remembering an irregular form.

summary: Ask whether you mean one or more than one, then choose the right plural.
A good puzzle mixes regular and irregular nouns.
Use the correct plural in speech so other people learn it too.

quiz.question: What is the plural of party?
What is the plural of birthday?
quiz.explanation: The letter before y is a vowel, so add -s only.

quiz.question: Which plural is irregular?
quiz.explanation: Children does not add -s or -es to child.

quiz.question: What is the plural of sheep?
quiz.explanation: Sheep has the same form in the singular and the plural.

quiz.question: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: Children is the plural of child, and songs is the regular plural of song.

quiz.question: Correct this phrase: two womans and a boxes.
quiz.explanation: Woman becomes women. A is singular, so box stays singular. If more than one box is meant, say boxes without a.

quiz.question: Which pair is correct?
options: person / persons as the usual plural
quiz.explanation: The usual plural of man is men. The usual plural of person is people.

quiz.question: Use men and prizes in one correct sentence.
quiz.answer: Any correct sentence, for example: The men gave prizes to the winners.
quiz.explanation: Men is irregular and prizes is regular.

quiz.question: A puzzle clue says "plural of glass". What is the answer?
quiz.explanation: Glass ends in s, so the plural adds -es.

quiz.question: Why should we use correct plurals when we speak?
quiz.answer: So listeners know how many people or things we mean, and so others hear the right form.
quiz.explanation: Childs and mans confuse the number and are not English plurals.
